entries.proposition: Genre and thesis: a review proposing that complement-mediated microglial pruning of intact synapses contributes to cognitive decline in paediatric DEE, built on rodent status epilepticus and human tissue.
entries.snippet: This represents an important time of neurodevelopment when resident brain cells use complement proteins to define and organize the architecture of the brain as well as construct functional neural circuitry [3].

experimental_context.system: narrative review of complement and microglia in paediatric epilepsy (rodent status epilepticus, adult and mixed-age human surgical tissue, CSF and serum biomarkers)

entries.proposition: The rodent evidence is from acute chemoconvulsant models of acquired status epilepticus at P14 and P21.
entries.snippet: research has shown through in vivo studies utilizing acute chemoconvulsant rodent models of acquired status epilepticus that abnormal activation of this process may be triggered by repeated episodes of early life seizure activity.

experimental_context.system: narrative review of complement and microglia in paediatric epilepsy (rodent status epilepticus, adult and mixed-age human surgical tissue, CSF and serum biomarkers)

entries.proposition: C3 knockout mice after severe status epilepticus showed less neurodegeneration and microglia-astrocyte interaction (cited).
entries.snippet: experimental data strongly demonstrates that complement-deficient (C3-/-) knockout mice subjected to severe status epilepticus exhibit a statistically significant reduction in histochemical neurodegeneration and pathological microglia–astrocyte interaction compared to wild-type mice [8].

entries.proposition: The human tissue evidence is mostly adult or mixed-age; the review cautions against extrapolating to paediatric DEE.
entries.snippet: Currently, much of the direct tissue evidence for complement activation in human epilepsy originates from adult or mixed-age surgical cohorts.

experimental_context.system: narrative review of complement and microglia in paediatric epilepsy (rodent status epilepticus, adult and mixed-age human surgical tissue, CSF and serum biomarkers)

entries.proposition: Human surgical tissue is cross-sectional, selected for pharmacoresistance, and cannot show whether complement is a driver or a consequence.
entries.snippet: Consequently, this observational data cannot definitively determine whether complement activation is a primary driver of the pathology or a secondary consequence of intractable seizures

experimental_context.system: narrative review of complement and microglia in paediatric epilepsy (rodent status epilepticus, adult and mixed-age human surgical tissue, CSF and serum biomarkers)

entries.proposition: Biomarker profiles differ by syndrome: acquired inflammatory syndromes versus genetic DEE (Dravet), and little evidence of complement activation in idiopathic generalised epilepsies.
entries.snippet: In contrast to severe encephalopathies, there is currently a lack of substantial evidence indicating significant complement activation in idiopathic generalized epilepsies (IGEs), such as childhood absence epilepsy [21].

experimental_context.system: narrative review of complement and microglia in paediatric epilepsy (rodent status epilepticus, adult and mixed-age human surgical tissue, CSF and serum biomarkers)

entries.proposition: Anti-seizure medications are described as not mitigating neuroinflammation, with cited preclinical data that phenobarbital or levetiracetam after status epilepticus did not consistently prevent chronic microglial activation.
entries.snippet: administering standard ASMs (such as phenobarbital or levetiracetam) during or immediately after status epilepticus generally suppresses acute convulsions but does not consistently prevent the subsequent development of spontaneous recurrent seizures or chronic microglial activation [32].
entries.anchor: 5.1. The Synaptic Gap in Current Care

entries.proposition: Neither named complement inhibitor has shown efficacy in paediatric epilepsy; their use in epilepsy is untested.
entries.snippet: Importantly, neither ANX005 nor pegcetacoplan has demonstrated efficacy in pediatric epilepsy or the prevention of seizure-associated synaptic pruning.

entries.snippet: As shown in Figure 2, targeted inhibition of C3 function in young mice results in reduced microglial CR3-mediated phagocytic activity on aberrantly tagged synaptic surfaces containing C3b.

entries.proposition: Safety: complement is part of general immune defence; blocking it in children may raise infection risk; encapsulated-organism prophylaxis and vaccination are the cited management.
entries.snippet: Children are still building their natural immunity and a suppressed complement pathway might increase a child’s risk for infections [45].

entries.snippet: Thus, if clinicians were to inhibit the complement system too soon or for too long, they would likely interfere with normal and healthy brain development.
